other_official_servers: Klaviyo documents a local MCP server variant and its environment-variable configuration alongside the hosted server; its repository and endpoint were not identified. https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/connect_to_the_klaviyo_mcp_server

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee or MCP-specific usage charge was found. Connection requires a Klaviyo account; the vendor does not state that MCP access itself is free.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Klaviyo lists a free plan with up to 250 active profiles and 500 monthly email sends; paid plans vary with product, profile count, and usage. The pricing page lists Email from $45/month and Email + SMS from $60/month for the displayed plan configuration.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The MCP documentation does not identify MCP-specific per-call pricing, credits, quotas, or rate limits. Klaviyo’s underlying plans have product-specific profile, email, and messaging limits.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Remote setup is documented for Klaviyo users with Owner, Admin, or Manager roles. Beta tools require beta=true. read-only, user-generated-content, toolsets, core-tools-only, and pagination query parameters affect the hosted tool surface. Listed Claude and ChatGPT apps do not support query parameters.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Klaviyo controls account roles, available tools, and OAuth authorization; the user/client controls documented connection query parameters where the client supports them.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with a Bearer challenge pointing to protected-resource metadata for /mcp. Metadata lists the endpoint as its own authorization server and bearer header transport. The authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code and refresh_token grants, S256 PKCE, dynamic registration, and client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and none token authentication. scopes_supported and token lifetime are absent from the provided metadata. D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official table labels tools Read Only or not and separately marks user-generated-content access. The reviewed page does not document MCP readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations. 2. read-only=true removes write-capable tools; the docs do not describe a general confirmation flow. One Beta tool, delete_agent_secret, says confirmation is required because dependent tools stop authenticating. Most advice to review calls is client-side guidance. 3. OAuth metadata lists no scopes_supported. Klaviyo account-role eligibility is Owner, Admin, or Manager; the docs do not state MCP token lifetime. The OAuth metadata advertises /token as revocation endpoint. 4. Query controls include read-only, user-generated-content disablement, beta, toolsets, core-tools-only, output schemas, and pagination. Docs describe local and remote variants; no production/sandbox or regional endpoints were found. 5. Klaviyo says the connector is intended for standard marketing data and not highly sensitive data such as card numbers; specific field masking is not documented. Some Beta secret-reading tools return masked values. 6. No MCP-specific call limits, quotas, or result truncation were found. paginate-lists and list-page-size control tool/list and other */list response pagination. 7. No MCP argument correction, coercion, or unknown-argument handling rules found. 8. Klaviyo API Logs can show MCP-originated calls and payloads; telemetry defaults and retention were not found. 9. report_unsupported_task invites reporting limitations to Klaviyo, only with consent to share prompt intent. No other feedback/rating/survey tool was identified. 10. No server-delivered skills identified. Docs give client-facing recommendations, including caution about malicious instructions in user-generated content. 11. No evidence that past agent behavior changes future tool availability or outputs. 12. The reviewed hosted endpoint is documented as one tool server; no nested servers or proxy architecture found. A separate local variant is documented. 13. No universal raw API request, SQL, script, or execution escape hatch identified in the 272 remote-listed tools.

E_aggregated.action_count: 190–272 documented remote tools, with an unquantified default core subset
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool list exists at https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server_available_tools and contains 274 unique tool names across local and remote availability; 272 are marked available remotely. Of those, 82 are marked Beta and require beta=true; 190 non-Beta tools are remote-listed. The docs also say the hosted server loads a core set by default but do not identify the core set or its exact count, so the exact default count is not established. The Claude connector directory is third-party, publisher-verified, and advertises 27 tools; its visible names are a subset of the official list. No catalogue-only action was added.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim initialize/tool-schema payload was available; the official table provides tool names, descriptions, and flags but not input schemas or initialize instructions.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The agent cannot perform operations absent from the MCP tool list; Klaviyo’s broader product and APIs include additional capabilities. The vendor states that this connector does not grant AI systems account modification in its Customer Success/Support engagement context; that statement is scoped to that service context. The hosted server tool list separately includes write tools. https://www.klaviyo.com/legal/ai-faqs https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server_available_tools

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Klaviyo instructs clients: “Be sure to carefully review each tool call to ensure your client is not acting on malicious instructions.” Its ChatGPT FAQ advises users to “always have a human in the loop to review and fact-check AI-generated content.” These are guidance to clients/users; no general server-enforced confirmation mechanism is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Klaviyo says the connector is “not intended to access highly sensitive data like credit card numbers or other highly sensitive PII.” It says API Logs can show tool calls, read/write status, and API calls and payloads. For ChatGPT, data retention is governed by OpenAI. For Claude, Klaviyo says processing is governed by the customer's agreements with Anthropic.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Klaviyo describes the server as connecting AI clients to its APIs and account data. For its Customer Success/Support engagement use, Klaviyo says MCP access is limited to data necessary for the requested service, does not permit account modification or automated actions, and is governed by applicable contractual and security commitments.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The documented read-only query parameter and tool availability flags back the ability to restrict writes. User-generated-content controls disable specific tools, while the malicious-instruction warning remains client guidance. API Logs provide some visibility, but logging defaults and retention are unspecified. The Customer Success/Support read-only statement is scoped to an active support engagement; the public hosted tool list includes write actions, so it does not describe the hosted server generally.

contradictions: The official tool reference says the hosted server loads a core set by default, while its query-parameter table gives core-tools-only a default of false and says disabling the parameter loads the full listed set. The exact default core set and count are not identified. https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server_available_tools https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/connect_to_the_klaviyo_mcp_server

The Klaviyo AI FAQ says MCP in the Customer Success/Support engagement context does not allow account modification or automated actions, while the public hosted tool reference lists write-capable tools. The FAQ statement is limited to its support-engagement context and should not be read as a claim about the general hosted endpoint. https://www.klaviyo.com/legal/ai-faqs https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server_available_tools

observations_for_research: The official tool reference distinguishes read-only status, user-generated-content access, and remote availability as separate tool properties.
The endpoint’s OAuth metadata supports dynamic registration and PKCE but publishes no scopes_supported list; toolsets can filter tools by required API scopes.
The tool reference labels 82 remote-listed tools Beta and the connection guide provides query parameters for read-only mode, user-generated-content exclusion, tool filtering, and pagination.
